newsitem.title: UK: Welcome Break pricing seen relatively generous -FT.
newsitem.headline: Welcome Break pricing seen relatively generous -FT.

text.p: Sources close to the multi-tranche sterling bond planned by INVESTCORP's Welcome Break said the pricing will be "relatively generous", the Financial Times newspaper said on Friday.
The FT quoted a firm involved in the deal as saying: "This won't be priced as widely as a high-yield issue, but on the other hand it will offer a wider spread than on standard A-rated deals".
Welcome Break, a chain of motorway service stations in Britain, was expected to raise around 320 million stg via a mix of fixed and floating-rate bonds in the near future.
There will be around 210 million stg of fixed-rate paper in two tranches with maturities of about 20 years.
The balance will be in 10- and 30-year FRNs.
The proceeds will repay loans taken out when Bahrain-based INVESTCORP paid Granada Group 476 million stg for Welcome Break in February.
Chase Manhattan and Bankers Trust, the joint lead managers, were not immediately available.
BZW will be a co-lead manager, dealers said.
